title: Ice & Snow
whatItIs: On ice and snow you have very little grip. Only drive if you must, and then do everything slowly and gently.

keyFacts.text: You MUST be able to see: clear all snow and ice from every window before you set off.
Lights MUST be clean and number plates clearly visible.

keyFacts: Stopping distances on ice can be up to ten times longer than on dry roads.
Use the highest gear you can, and accelerate and brake very gently.
Brake on the straight before a bend, then steer smoothly round it.
Very quiet tyres and light steering can mean you are on ice.

items.title: Clear everything first
items.text: Windows, lights and number plates by law. Clear the mirrors and the snow on the roof too.

items.title: Slow and gentle
items.text: High gear, low revs, gentle on the accelerator, brakes and steering.

items.title: Brake before bends
items.text: Slow down on the straight, then steer smoothly round.

items.title: Signs of ice
items.text: Tyres go quiet and the steering feels light.

onTheTest.question: You are driving on an icy road. How can you avoid wheelspin?
options: Use the highest gear you can
Use first gear and high revs
onTheTest.why: A high gear and gentle acceleration send less power to the wheels, so they are less likely to spin.

traps: Clear the whole windscreen, not just a small hole to see through.
Low gear and high revs make the wheels spin on ice.
Brake before the bend, not while you are in it.
